title: Comparison of robot-assisted and conventionally instrumented total knee arthroplasty in patients with advanced knee osteoarthritis – a retrospective cohort study
summary: People with advanced knee osteoarthritis may receive an artificial knee joint. This study compares two established surgical techniques using already available clinical data. The aim is to investigate possible differences in knee function, duration of surgery, implant positioning and complications. No additional examinations are performed and no new data are collected.

interventions.name: Robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty for advanced knee osteoarthritis using the VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution. Only routinely collected clinical data are retrospectively analysed.

Conventionally instrumented total knee arthroplasty: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty for advanced knee osteoarthritis using conventional instrumentation without robotic assistance. Only routinely collected clinical data are retrospectively analysed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Primary knee osteoarthritis requiring primary total knee arthroplasty.
• Primary implantation of a total knee arthroplasty using either the VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution or conventional instrumentation.
• Surgery performed between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2025.
• Age ≥18 years.
• Complete clinical documentation including preoperative and postoperative OKS assessment and radiographic follow-up.
Exclusion criteria:
• Revision total knee arthroplasty.
• Total knee arthroplasty performed for fracture, tumour or inflammatory joint disease.
• Incomplete clinical documentation.
• Missing OKS data or missing radiographic follow-up.
• Missing essential study data.
